DashboardEvent.description:
One entry in the important-events strip -- a merged, time-ordered
projection of M1.139's `/news` and `/events` feeds (the same merge
the Flutter M1.140 UI already does client-side, done once here
server-side so the dashboard needs only one request).
DashboardEvent.title: DashboardEvent

DashboardOpportunity.description:
One top-opportunity summary card, per EPIC-M3.2's API Contract field
list. A deliberately leaner projection of M1.135's `RecommendationSummary`
-- only the fields the EPIC names, plus `id` -- not a second, divergent
recommendation representation (the underlying row is the exact same one
`/recommendations` returns). `id` is the one addition beyond the EPIC's
own "must expose at minimum" list: the Acceptance Criteria requires
"navigation into full opportunity/detail views", which is impossible
without an identifier for the existing `/recommendation/:id` detail
route -- an honest, necessary extension, not a contract violation
("at minimum" permits additional fields).
DashboardOpportunity.title: DashboardOpportunity

DashboardTrustSummary.description:
A compact projection of M1.147's `/tracking/summary` -- only the
fields relevant to a one-glance trust widget. Not a recomputation:
every value here is read verbatim from `TrackingSummary`.
DashboardTrustSummary.title: DashboardTrustSummary

DataFreshness.description:
Per-section as-of timestamps so a viewer can tell which parts of the
snapshot are current vs. stale, without fabricating a single combined
number across sources that update on different cadences.
DataFreshness.title: DataFreshness

DiscoveryCandidate.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/discovery/candidates` -- the same discovery
universe as `DiscoveryItem` above, reprojected with an explicit
lifecycle stage and (only for an authenticated caller) a suppression
reason, per EPIC-M3.6. Suppressed is never a negative/bearish call --
it only means this candidate did not clear the positive-opportunity
bar this cycle.

`candidateId` is the underlying `DiscoveryRecord.id` (EPIC-M3.6's own
field name for it). The EPIC's `providerEvidence` and `qualification`
fields are deliberately not separate keys here -- they are already
served, without inventing a second representation, by
`discoveryReasons` (the provider's own rationale text) and
`score`/`trustScore` (the qualification signal) respectively.
`publishedRecommendationId` is only set once `lifecycleStage` reaches
`PUBLISHED`, letting a client link straight to `/recommendation/:id`.
DiscoveryCandidate.title: DiscoveryCandidate

DiscoverySourceEffectiveness.description:
Per-source discovery effectiveness, reprojected verbatim from
EPIC-M1.28's `app.discovery_effectiveness.DiscoverySourceFunnel` --
no new scoring/verdict logic, just camelCase field names for the API.
DiscoverySourceEffectiveness.title: DiscoverySourceEffectiveness

DisplayPreferences.description:
Free-form key/value display settings (e.g. theme, density). No
domain module owns display concerns, so this is validated only as a
JSON object -- values are opaque to the API layer.
DisplayPreferences.title: DisplayPreferences

EvidenceResponse.description:
EPIC-M3.4: the fundamental/technical/market/news/event evidence
sections plus provider provenance, as their own contract -- the same
values already embedded in `RecommendationDetail`, projected out so a
caller only interested in evidence doesn't have to fetch the full
detail payload.
EvidenceResponse.title: EvidenceResponse

FeedbackHistoryItem.description:
One row of ``GET /api/v1/feedback/history`` (EPIC-M3.10).

Field names follow M3.10's own "Feedback model" list
(``feedbackId``/``recommendationId``/``predictionVersionId``/
``reasonCode``/``note``/``createdAt``) with one deliberate
substitution: M3.10's illustrative ``rating`` is realized here as
``type`` -- the exact ``useful``/``not_useful``/``target_*``/``reason``
vocabulary EPIC-M1.141 already established for submission (see
``VALID_FEEDBACK_TYPES`` above). There is no separate numeric rating
scale anywhere in this codebase; reusing the real submitted vocabulary
is honest where inventing a new, unbacked rating enum would not be.
``predictionVersionId`` holds the same ``model_version`` string
accepted by ``FeedbackRequest.predictionVersion``, not a surrogate id
-- no separate prediction-version id exists.
FeedbackHistoryItem.title: FeedbackHistoryItem

Freshness.description:
How stale the newest successful fetch is against M1.35's own
`FRESHNESS_POLICY` threshold for this capability -- never a fabricated
single number across capabilities with different real cadences.
Freshness.title: Freshness

IndexQuote.description:
Shape reserved for future index-level data. Always empty for now --
this platform ingests individual NSE equity prices only, no index
(e.g. NIFTY50) feed exists, so fabricating a value here would be
dishonest rather than merely incomplete.
IndexQuote.title: IndexQuote

LearningHistoryEntry.description:
One event in the unified learning-history timeline. `id` is a
composite `"<source-table>:<row id>"` string (not a single row's own
primary key) since this feed merges rows from several distinct,
independently-keyed tables -- never a fabricated shared sequence.
LearningHistoryEntry.title: LearningHistoryEntry

LearningSignalSummary.description:
One (category, reason_code) feedback pattern, reprojected verbatim
from `app.feedback_learning_signals.FeedbackSignal` -- camelCase DTO
only, no new scoring/verdict logic.
LearningSignalSummary.title: LearningSignalSummary

LoginRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (EPIC-M3.12). ``userId`` is
verified by whichever ``CredentialVerifier`` this deployment configures
(see ``app.auth_session``); the default, until a real identity provider
is integrated, is self-asserted.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

OpportunityFilters.description:
Echoes back exactly the filters/sort this response was computed
with (AC: filter combinations are server-side and deterministic --
a client should never have to guess what was actually applied).
OpportunityFilters.title: OpportunityFilters

PredictionVersions.description: Every version tag needed to replay how this recommendation was produced.
PredictionVersions.title: PredictionVersions

TimelineItem.description:
EPIC-M3.4: full, ordered prediction-version timeline -- the
original prediction plus every immutable revision, each carrying its
own reason and the specific metrics it changed. Distinct from
`/history` (paginated, revisions-only) by always including version 1
(the original) so a caller can reconstruct the *entire* lifecycle in
one call, not just what changed after it.
TimelineItem.title: TimelineItem
